chunks: ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr asked him and said:
I have made it binding upon myself to fast until al-Qāʾim عليه السلام rises.
He said: “Do not fast during travel, nor on the two ʿEids, nor on the days of Tashrīq, nor on the day about which there is doubt.”

key_terms.أَصُومَ: to fast as an act of worship
key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: the days of Tashrīq, during which fasting is prohibited in this ruling
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, during which fasting is not to be observed here
key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: the two ʿEids on which fasting is forbidden
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: the Qa'im, the awaited Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الَّذِي يُشَكُّ فِيهِ: the day of doubt, when the start of the month is uncertain

ai.seo_question: Does a vow to fast continuously include days on which fasting is forbidden?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a vow to fast continuously until the rise of al-Qāʾim عليه السلام. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies that such a vow does not override the prohibited times of fasting, including travel, the two ʿEids, the days of Tashrīq, and the doubtful day.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1925 - Abd al-Karim ibn Amr asked Imam (as): "I have made a vow upon myself to fast until the Qa'im (as) rises."
Imam (as) said: "Do not fast during travel, on the two Eids, on the days of Tashriq, or on the day of doubt."
